instruction.text: There is a conflict between Peter and Lisa. Select Lisa’s phone to hear what is going on.

feedback.end: Peter is annoyed with Lisa because she is on her phone at dinner.

instruction.text: What do you think Peter is thinking right now? Listen and choose.

b.sound: I wish Lisa would talk to me instead of looking at her phone.
I don’t want to talk to Lisa. I am glad she is on her phone.

instruction.text: What could Lisa be thinking right now? Listen and choose.

b.sound: I think somebody texted me. I had better answer the message right away.
My phone is boring and I hate looking at it.

instruction.text: What would an agreement look like? Listen and choose the correct description.

b.sound: Peter asks Lisa to put her phone away at dinner, and she agrees.
Peter takes Lisa’s phone and turns it off.

instruction.text: Do you remember the ways to solve a conflict? Listen to the explanation and select the matching image.

atoms.a: If two or more people want to have the same thing, they can share the thing or take turns.
If someone makes you sad or angry, you could just go somewhere else.
If someone did something unfair or mean to someone else, apologising may help to solve the conflict.
